names.display_en: Fu Jian (Jian), Founder of Former Qin

summary: 苻洪之子，统众入关据长安，自称天王、大单于，国号大秦，旋称帝；皇始中坚壁清野拒桓温北伐，前秦基业始固；皇始五年崩，子生继而残虐。
summary_en: Son of Fu Hong, he led the host into the pass, took Chang'an, styled himself Heavenly King and Great Chanyu of the realm Great Qin, then emperor; in mid-Huangshi he denied Huan Wen's expedition by clearing the land, and the Qin foundations were set. He died in the 5th year of Huangshi, his cruel son Sheng succeeding.

portrait.appearance_basis: 史载无形貌描写。画像宜表现审时度势的开国之君之态，衣冠从氐族入华制。属艺术想象。

timeline.title: 生
timeline.summary_en: Son of Fu Hong, styled Jianye, a Di of Lüeyang.

timeline.title: 入关中
timeline.summary: 洪死，健统众入关，据长安。
timeline.summary_en: Hong died; Jian led the host into the pass and took Chang'an.

timeline.title: 称天王
timeline.summary: 自称天王、大单于，国号大秦，都长安。
timeline.summary_en: He styled himself Heavenly King and Great Chanyu of the realm Great Qin, with his capital at Chang'an.

timeline.title: 称帝
timeline.summary_en: He took the imperial throne and installed his officials.

timeline.title: 桓温北伐拒之
timeline.summary: 桓温入关，健坚壁清野，温粮尽退。
timeline.summary_en: Huan Wen entered the pass; Jian cleared the land and held his walls until Wen's grain ran out and he withdrew.

timeline.title: 苻健崩
timeline.summary: 崩，子生继，残虐；后苻坚杀生自立。
timeline.summary_en: He died; his son Sheng, a cruel tyrant, succeeded; later Fu Jian (the Great Ancestor's nephew) slew Sheng and took the throne.

relations.note: 苻坚（侄）杀苻生后为前秦雄主，淝水败亡
relations.note_en: Fu Jian (his nephew) kills Fu Sheng and becomes the great ruler of Former Qin, then falls after the defeat at Fei River

bio_md:
# 前秦高祖 · 主要事迹

苻健字建业，略阳氐人，苻洪第三子。苻洪为后赵所害，健统其众。永和六年，健率众自枋头入关，击破杜洪，据长安；皇始元年，自称天王、大单于，国号大秦，都长安；皇始二年，即皇帝位。前秦立国之基，自苻健始。

皇始中，东晋桓温北伐，入关至霸上，关中震恐。苻健坚壁清野，尽收其麦，温军粮尽而退——「健以逸待劳」，遂保关中。苻健在位五年，抚流民、劝农桑、置百官，「虽戎狄之俗，渐染华风」。皇始五年，健崩，谥景明皇帝。其子苻生继位，残暴无道，旋为侄苻坚所杀——前秦之大业，终落于苻坚之手。

苻健以氐族之身，乘乱据关中，为前秦开创基业；其拒桓温之役，尤见将略。然健虽开基，未及大治，子生之暴、侄坚之兴，皆其身后之事。前秦自苻坚始成为十六国最强者，然其根柢，实植于苻健之世。

> 参考：点校本《晋书》卷112《苻健载记》、卷113《苻坚载记》。

bio_parts_en.value:
Fu Jian, styled Jianye, was a Di of Lüeyang, third son of Fu Hong. When Fu Hong was done to death by Later Zhao, Jian took command of his host. In the 6th year of Yonghe he led his men through the pass, broke Du Hong, and took Chang'an; in the 1st year of Huangshi he styled himself Heavenly King and Great Chanyu of the realm Great Qin with his capital at Chang'an; in the 2nd year he took the imperial throne. The foundations of Former Qin were laid by Jian.

In mid-Huangshi, Huan Wen of Eastern Jin campaigned north and entered the pass, reaching Bashan, and Guanzhong was shaken. Jian cleared the land of its grain and held his walls; Wen's army ran out of food and withdrew — "Jian, at ease, wore the invader out," and Guanzhong was saved. In five years he gathered the refugees, encouraged farming, and installed his officials, "the barbarian custom gradually taking on Chinese ways." He died in the 5th year of Huangshi, posthumously Emperor Jingming. His son Sheng succeeded, a cruel tyrant, and was soon slain by his nephew Fu Jian — the great enterprise of Former Qin passed to the nephew.

A Di who seized Guanzhong in the chaos and founded Former Qin, Jian showed real generalship in denying Huan Wen. He founded the state but did not live to perfect it; the tyrant Sheng and the rise of Fu Jian were the work of his successors. Former Qin became the strongest of the Sixteen States under Fu Jian — but its roots were planted in Jian's reign.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Jinshu*, ch. 112 (records of Fu Jian), ch. 113 (records of Fu Jian the Great Ancestor).
